findings.message: Default camera at (8.5,7,7.5) looks almost along the ball's descent direction from (2.4,1.6) to the centre, so the Downhill step and Noisy step arrows are foreshortened to a tiny stub at the ball and cannot be read; the side view shows them clearly. Move the default camera to look across the descent path (e.g. nearer the side angle) and frame ball, arrows and flag larger.
The 'Noisy step' and 'Downhill step' labels are stacked next to arrows much smaller than the labels themselves, so the labels name objects the learner cannot see.

The plan says to drag the ball to any starting point on the surface, but the drag only moves it along w1 (disclosed). The trail also adds a point every step instead of the plan's every 2 steps (disclosed). Dragging was not sampled.

After 40 steps the noisy path toward the minimum looks like a short squiggle in the default view, because the camera looks along the path. The trail is the main result and fills only a few dozen pixels, while the side view shows it clearly. Re-aim or fit the default camera to the path region.

Near the minimum the arrows are tiny but their 'Downhill step' and 'Noisy step' labels stay full size and sit over the ball, flag and end of the trail, hiding the settling behaviour. Hide or shrink the labels when the arrows are short, or move them away.
The Status text readout ('diverged') is not shown in the readout bar; only loss and steps appear, so the divergence verdict is only visible from the ball leaving the bowl.
The default camera problem is the same as in v0-s0 and v0-s1: the arrows and path in normal runs are foreshortened. This capture itself is readable as a zig-zag that leaves the bowl.

In the default view the two step arrows are short (about 1.6 units at 4× scale) and almost on top of each other, partly hidden behind the ball. The 'Downhill step' and 'Noisy step' labels are bigger than the arrows they name, and 'Downhill step' sits right against the 'Minimum' label. Draw the arrows longer with a single disclosed scale and spread them apart (for example a larger A, or a camera closer to the ball), and move the labels so they don't crowd each other or the Minimum label.

At the default state the bowl fills less than half the frame, with wide empty margins on every side, so the ball, arrows and labels (the actual subject) are small. Bring the camera closer so the bowl and the ball's path fill the view.
The plan lets the learner drag the ball to any start point on the surface. The artifact limits dragging to w1 only (this is disclosed). The drag interaction was not sampled.
Near the minimum the ball covers the flag pole and the arrows are too short to see. This is acceptable, but the flag base is hidden.
The Status text readout ('diverged') is missing from the readout bar in the capture, which shows only Loss and Steps taken. The divergence is still visible from the ball leaving the bowl.
The 'Minimum' label sits over the dense zig-zag trail lines.
The low-end learning rate, the noise=0 smooth path, the stretch extremes, clear trail, new run and drag were not sampled.
